title: Square Face Shape: Features, Hair, Glasses & Makeup Guide
summary: Learn how to identify a square face shape and explore hairstyles, glasses, makeup, and beard ideas that complement strong, angular features.
body_markdown:
### What are the main features of a square face shape?


A square face shape often has similar width across the forehead, cheekbones, and jawline, along with a strong, angular jaw and a broad or flatter chin. Many people have blended traits, so these features are best treated as a general guide.


### How can I tell if I have a square face shape?


Compare your forehead, cheekbone, and jaw widths in a front-facing mirror or photo. If they look relatively even and your jawline appears angular rather than rounded or pointed, you may have a square face shape. Use our[face shape test guide](https://www.perfectcorp.com/business/blog/general/face-shape-test) for a broader comparison of categories.


### What hairstyles suit a square face shape?


Soft layers, waves, side parts, curtain fringe, rounded bobs, and textured cuts are popular options when you want softer framing. Sleek or structured styles can also look intentional when you want to emphasize the face’s angular shape.


### What glasses suit a square face shape?


Round, oval, cat-eye, and softly curved frames can create contrast with an angular jawline. Geometric or rectangular frames can also work when they match your preferred style. Comfort, fit, lens size, and personal preference should guide the final choice.


### Is a square face shape attractive?


No face shape is inherently more or less attractive than another. Square faces are often associated with defined facial structure, but style choices should be based on personal preference—not a fixed beauty standard.


### Can AI identify a square face shape?


A photo-based AI tool can compare visible facial proportions and attributes with common face-shape categories. Results can vary with lighting, image angle, hair, expression, and the natural overlap between face shapes, so they are best used as a styling reference.
